title: The Lady in Black by Eleanor H. Porter
topic: A silent clock and a boy's cry reveal a mother's private grief.

source.author: VOA Learning English
source.license: Public domain (work of the US federal government)

body: The house was very still. In the little room over the porch, the Lady in Black sat alone. Near her, a child’s white dress lay across a chair. On the floor at her feet lay a tiny pair of shoes. A doll hung over a chair and a toy soldier occupied the little stand by the bed.
And everywhere was silence—the strange silence that comes only to a room where the clock has stopped ticking.

The clock stood on the shelf near the end of the bed. The Lady in Black looked at it. She remembered the wave of anger that had come over her when she had reached out her hand and silenced the clock that night three months before.

It had been silent ever since and it should remain silent, too. Of what possible use were the hours it would tick away now? As if anything mattered, with little Kathleen lying out there white and still under the black earth!

The Lady in Black moved restlessly and looked toward the closed door. Behind it, she knew, was a little boy with wide blue eyes who wanted her. But she wished he would not call her by that name. It only reminded her of those other little lips--silent now.
The Lady in Black did not answer. He might go away, she thought, if she did not answer.

previewWords.gloss: in an uneasy way, unable to stay still

quiz.q: Why did the Lady in Black stop the clock three months earlier?
options: she was angry after her daughter's death
the clock was broken beyond repair
she wanted to save it as a gift

quiz.q: Who is calling 'Muvver' from behind the closed door?
How does the Lady in Black respond when the voice calls again?
options: she calls out for him to come in
she stays silent, hoping he will go away
she opens the door right away
